writing: What I learned as the only Somali in a Big 4 apprenticeship cohort
Agentic AI is not what your LinkedIn feed says it is
Why I'm betting on enterprise AI strategy, not pure engineering

about.opening: I design and build agentic AI systems. Senior Solutions Architect at EY, working at the intersection of AI, automation, and enterprise data. I am a strategist who can build, and a builder who thinks in strategy.

sections.heading: The Path
sections.body: I started at EY at 19 as one of the few Somali apprentices in a Big 4 firm in Birmingham. I was promoted twice, from Digital Apprentice to Solutions Developer to Senior Solutions Architect. Today I ship AI tooling and audit automation at scale inside EY's Data and Intelligence Delivery Centre of Excellence.

sections.heading: What I Build
sections.body: Outside of EY, I build agentic AI systems. Voice-first agents, LLM-orchestrated workflows, the kind of tools that turn manual processes into infrastructure. I work with the modern AI stack: Anthropic, Vapi, ElevenLabs, Make.com, Twilio.

sections.heading: What I'm Working Toward
sections.body: Enterprise AI strategy. Specifically, the intersection of AI capability, regulatory governance, and commercial outcomes. The kind of work that sits between the partners who own the relationship and the engineers who build the system.

sections.heading: Outside Work
sections.body: Born and based in Birmingham. Away from the screen I play a lot of sport, get outdoors whenever I can, and travel to experience new places and cultures. I like trying things I have not done before, it tends to be where the most interesting ideas come from. Family and community matter to me.

beliefs: Strategy without the ability to build is theatre.
Quiet output beats loud positioning, eventually.
Stay curious. The best work comes from trying things you have not done before.
